### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via registerApp (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL), registerObject (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry), /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class), /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c42de6639a0275cade2bd652ea0073cb6ebc06b8` — the merge of head `f72ef4f72c41e360be5fced77465bc68b23a1c7a` into base `663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c42de6639a0275cade2bd652ea0073cb6ebc06b8 && git checkout c42de6639a0275cade2bd652ea0073cb6ebc06b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415 f72ef4f72c41e360be5fced77465bc68b23a1c7a && git checkout -B drift-repro 663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415 && git merge --no-ff f72ef4f72c41e360be5fced77465bc68b23a1c7a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 663b7c08eedd61a3a492a425ced0dbbd57676415` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f72ef4f72c41e360be5fced77465bc68b23a1c7a`
Local-runs: none

Face: the committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path (`record-recognisers --paths` on the seven changed files decides no path face and defers to the changeset's declaration line), and the declaration carries no `(narrowing)` arm, so the review is owed on the declaration face alone and is served at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read at 2026-11-01T22:02Z, read-only: card #28697 (the claim and the os-dev-report), PR #28822 (body, five commits, the net diff against the merge-base `c064d3a2`: seven files, +569 / −12), PR #28790 (merged `899782b5`) with both records on it, the cited code on the head and on `origin/main`. Nothing built, run or re-run. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. Check-runs on the head at the read: 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Test UI` are success; `Build Core`, the eight Test Core shards, three lint lanes, three type-check lanes and Live E2E UI are in progress. Landing pre-check ② (all green) is not met yet at this read; the seat re-reads at landing. Draft, mergeable; no `needs:contract-review` marker was hung.

Security class: verdicts in product words. Mechanism detail, the write-by-write completeness table and the follow-up observations are in a private note with the seat.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A refused upgrade leaves the installed version serving, whole.** When a package id that is already installed is re-registered and the registry refuses the new version at any point of the registration, what the engine serves afterwards reads exactly as before the attempt: the package record and its version, every object as served and as layered, every app and item, picklist options and extensions, namespaces, security-catalog names, default record page holders, the engine's package entry and datasource routing. I read every registry state field against the write sites the registration reaches, and each one the registration can write is recorded before its first write and put back on a throw; the engine's own entries were already written only after a whole registration and still are. Another package's extension of the installed version's objects and a tenant's overlay layer are put back as the same entries, unchanged. Entries the registration did not write are neither recorded nor touched, so other packages' and tenants' entries do not move. **Right.** Pinned for every refusal the registry can raise during an upgrade (ten unit cases, one dogfood case through `POST /marketplace/install-local`), each asserting the same code and status as before and a whole-state equality with the reading taken before the attempt.
2. **Not through uninstall, and safe.** The restore calls no removal verb; it puts entries back in place. The registration it runs is synchronous by contract (a body that returned a promise is refused, and what the synchronous part wrote is still put back), a nested call joins the open run, no hook or listener exists on the registry to re-enter it, and every undo step is a plain container operation that cannot itself throw. The restore applies only to an installed id, and PR #28790's withdrawal applies only to an id that is not installed, so the two paths are disjoint by construction and a first install keeps #28790's behaviour unchanged (its file reads 24/24 with exactly one control flipped into the new behaviour). **Right.**
3. **The choice to build the restore without the ahead-judgment.** The order asked the dev to measure which part-way refusals can be judged before the registry's first write before choosing, and preferred judging ahead where possible. The measured split is in the private hand-back: half of the part-way refusals depend on registry state and need the restore whatever else is built, and with the restore in place judging the rest ahead changes no outcome for an upgrade, would be an unpinned second call site of each judge, and would change which of two faults a body is refused for. The stop condition was not needed. I read the order's preference as one to weigh against the measurement it demanded, and the measurement supports the restore alone for the in-scope path. **Acceptable;** the os-dev-report's open question is answered under ③.
4. **No change to what is refused or its words.** Every refusal keeps its code, status and message (each case pins code and status; the dogfood case pins the message); nothing is newly refused and nothing refused is admitted. **Right.**
5. **The new public method.** One public method on the published `SchemaRegistry`, taking one synchronous registration and returning its result; the journal and its record points are private. That is the minimal door the engine needs, since the record points have to sit inside the registry's own verbs. The doc comment is accurate on what is recorded, on what is never recorded (the operator's removal verbs), on the synchronous contract and on nesting; one phrase ("re-resolved") is loosely worded for a cache drop. A third party calling it gets what it says: a restore of registry writes, nothing for a removal verb, and a clear error for an async body. The spec contract the engine exposes its registry through is structural and still satisfied. The shared registry test double runs the body as given, which is right for a double that never answers an installed package. **Right.**
6. **Controls and ablations** (as reported, not re-run): a clean upgrade behaves as before and keeps the other package's extension and the tenant overlay; a refusal the package door raises before its first write leaves the installed version as before; the other package's own entries do not move; red-first on the base engine, registry and double reds exactly the ten upgrade cases plus the flipped control (each passing its code-and-status assertion and failing at the state comparison) and the dogfood case; ten ablations each red exactly the cases that reach the record point removed, the re-resolve ablation included. The counts match which cases reach which record point in the fixture as I read it. **Consistent with the diff.**
7. **Evidence left to CI.** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was NOT MEASURED locally (it needs every package's build output); it is a step of the `Build Core` job, in progress on the head at the read. The remaining 67 derived gate families exited 0 in the dev's record, with 0 unrun.
8. **Overlap and drift.** Of the 33 open PRs at the read, only #28811 (draft) touches one of the four files, `registry.ts`, in hunks away from this PR's (a refusal block at the top of the object verb and new extension verbs further down); no textual overlap, and the one semantic touch point is consistent with this PR's documented contract. `origin/main` moved the engine and registry once since the merge-base (#28791); the branch merges clean. **No conflict.**

### ② Semver level

One changeset, `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with a dash-clause naming the one new public method on the published `SchemaRegistry`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. Both declarations are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. AGENTS.md rule 3: the level follows the protocol kind alone, so `none` keeps `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads `yes (widening)` + `none` + `patch` as consistent and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The diff enlarges the public surface by exactly that one method and changes nothing an author can write; the spec's engine contract is untouched. No `(narrowing)` arm and no spec path, so the face is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`. **Consistent.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Boundary change.** Nothing newly refused, nothing refused admitted; only what a refused upgrade leaves behind changes. Public surface: one new method (②).
- **Order rulings.** A refused upgrade leaves the installed version serving, whole, with other packages' extensions and tenant overlays intact: met (① 1). Not through uninstall: met (① 2). The split measured before choosing, the restore of exactly the touched entries built, the ahead-judgment left out with the reason recorded: acceptable reading (① 3). No change to refusal codes or words: met (① 4). First installs keep #28790's withdrawal: met (① 2). The stop condition was not reached.
- **Dev flags and `open_questions`.** One open question: also judge the body-only refusals ahead of the first write (A: restore only, this PR; B: a separate card for the one first-install case the private hand-back names). Answered: A for this PR (① 3); B only if the seat wants that first-install case closed, as a separate card, since it flips one of #28790's controls. One out-of-scope finding, the same first-install case: correctly left out, the order scopes this PR to upgrades and keeps first installs on #28790's behaviour; its existing control pins it.
- **Security class.** The PR body, commits and changeset are in product words; nothing in them reads as a recipe. One optional trim for the seat is named in the private note. The test sources enumerate the cases they pin, as any test of a fix does; noted, acceptable.
- **CI state.** 0 failures; `Build Core` (which hosts the one locally unmeasured gate), the Test Core shards, three lint lanes, three type-check lanes and Live E2E UI in progress at the read; landing pre-check ② is the seat's at landing.
- **File surface and author.** Seven files, inside the claim's surface; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft, no auto-merge.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-cjuysm`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**

No must-fix. Should-fix, none required before landing: the one optional body trim and the doc-comment wording are in the private note with the seat.
